findings.text: follow-on: begin_discovery at reckon/serve.py:2286 is not paired with flush_discovery at :2385 in a try/finally, so an exception raised anywhere in the document loop leaves the batch entry in metadata_index._DISCOVERY_BATCHES and silently drops that pass's recorded parses; the next begin_discovery on the same (docs_dir, project) key replaces it rather than nesting, so the loss is bounded to one pass re-parsed by the following read, not an unbounded leak, and nothing corrupt is persisted — recorded for the discipline, not a reason to hold the node.

follow-on: the comment "writes the store once per document exactly as it did before the batch" narrates the pre-change behaviour, the changelog phrasing the repository's naming rules exclude from source; :139 ("the defect the batch removes") reads the same way. Both describe the mechanism adequately without the temporal reference and are worth rewriting in place, but neither affects behaviour and neither is a banned token.
